headline: Bello Shutout Relief Not Enough As Sox Drop Opener In Cleveland
morning_brew: What a disaster of a start in Cleveland. We spot the Guardians four runs in the very first inning and spend the rest of the night playing catch-up. Tyler Samaniego had a brutal outing, lasting only one inning and giving up six hits. But let's talk about Brayan Bello. Coming out of the bullpen, Bello was absolutely sensational, tossing seven shutout innings and racking up five strikeouts to keep us in the game.

The offense did their best to claw back, racking up eleven hits in total, but we just could not deliver the knockout blow. We scored three runs in the fifth inning and then completely went cold. I been sayin' it all year, you cannot leave that many runners on base and expect to win on the road. Mickey Gasper and Isiah Kiner-Falefa both had solid nights with two hits each, but it was not enough. This four to three loss drops our record to twenty-three and thirty-three, keeping us stuck at the bottom of the division.

Now that the Bruins are officially in off-season mode, the focus shifts to how this front office is going to retool. The latest free agency tiers are out, and there are some serious impact players hitting the market in July. After that disappointing first-round exit, we cannot have another summer of standing pat. Management needs to be aggressive on the phones because this fan base is not going to tolerate another year of early exits.
